actions.action: Lock selections instead of deleting them
actions.mechanism: A private resume code separates access protection from ticket retention without creating an account.
actions.implementation: Before selection, establish a masked six-digit code. After 90 idle seconds, hide selections and stop personalized speech; retain an encrypted local draft for 30 minutes.
actions.check: Pause five minutes, then recover identical tickets using the code. Incorrect codes must reveal nothing; enforce kiosk-wide attempt limits.
actions.risk: Forgotten codes, shoulder surfing, and attempt-limit lockouts remain possible.

actions.action: Keep reading material outside the private session
actions.mechanism: Untimed, nonpersonal information remains readable while ticket selections stay locked separately.
actions.implementation: Move ticket descriptions, eligibility explanations, and instructions into public reading screens. Never include selected quantities or personal details. Preserve their reading position through locking.
actions.check: Spend several minutes reading each screen using touch and screen reader. Information remains available, while opening selections requires unlocking.
actions.risk: Separating descriptions from selections adds navigation and memory demands.

actions.action: Make starting fresh an explicit privacy boundary
actions.mechanism: Starting another visit clears the entire presentation state without exposing or overwriting a protected draft.
actions.implementation: Provide an always-available Start new visit control. Atomically clear selections, form values, navigation history, and queued speech before rendering the new flow.
actions.check: Start fresh from every screen, then press physical Back and Confirm. Neither display nor speech may expose previous content or submit anything.
actions.risk: Accidental restarts require code-based recovery of the previous draft.

actions.action: Collect personal details only at the end
actions.mechanism: Separating tickets from personal details limits what survives an interruption.
actions.implementation: Request only necessary details after ticket selection. On locking or restarting, delete entered personal details, retaining ticket choices only; explain that details require re-entry.
actions.check: Interrupt every personal-data field and inspect subsequent screens, speech, logs, and restored drafts. Tickets survive; entered details do not.
actions.risk: Visitors interrupted during data entry must repeat that portion.

actions.action: Keep recovery local and submission explicitly gated
actions.mechanism: Local drafts survive network loss; reconnection cannot silently turn a draft into a purchase.
actions.implementation: Store encrypted drafts and cached ticket information locally. After recovery, require a fresh review and explicit confirmation. If offline payment is unsupported, preserve tickets and explain the limitation.
actions.check: Disconnect for ten minutes, lock, restart, and recover. Reconnecting must submit nothing without confirmation; retries of an explicitly confirmed purchase must not duplicate it.
actions.risk: Final payment may require connectivity; restored availability needs validation.

actions.mechanism: Content-free event measurements expose whether privacy protection creates excessive recovery work.
actions.implementation: Record lock counts, recovery success, re-entry counts, and completion time without codes or personal content. Test slow reading and scripted abandonment using synthetic purchases.
actions.check: Compare against the 90-second reset: measure reconstructed selections and completion, plus disclosure duration before locking and any disclosure after locking or Start new visit.
actions.risk: The idle interval still permits exposure before locking; report it explicitly.
